course_summary:
ISEN 640 | Systems Thinking and Analysis | Fall 2026
Instructor: Joseph Geunes | geunes@tamu.edu, Richard Mayer | ricmayer@tamu.edu
Meets: M 6:00PM - 8:30PM | ZACH 160
Grading: Exam 1 (Midterm) [25%], Exam 2 (Final) [25%], Homework (assignments & quizzes) [50%] — A: 90% - 100%, B: 80% - 89.9%, C: 70% - 79.9%, D: 60% - 69.9%, F: below 60%
Topics: Complex Adaptive Systems Definition, Model Based Systems Engineering, Model Based Decision Making, Systems Description Languages, Theory of Systems Design, System Architectures, Engineered Systems Life Cycle, Documenting the SE Process, systems thinking process, engineering of large-scale systems, anatomy of engineered systems, complex interactions, formulate issues, analyze issues, interpret issues, separate symptoms, separate concerns, separate opportunities, diagnose causes, identify causes (problem), systems thinking techniques, systems thinking methods, systems engineering practice, critical thinking techniques, model engineered systems, critique engineered systems, analyze engineered systems, systems engineering methods, multidisciplinary teams, communicate ideas (verbally), communicate ideas (in writing), national systems engineering issues, global systems engineering issues, Development, Systems Modeling, Modeling, Systems Thinking in Engineering Design, Trade-offs, Systems Thinking and Analysis
Tools: software tools, Canvas, Zoom
Prerequisites: MATH 304 or approval of instructor
